# WhyUser

> WhyUser is pre-launch buyer simulation for B2B marketing teams. It builds buyer personas from the customer's own buyers' words (reviews, community threads, buyer questions, sales calls, CRM objections, win/loss notes), then runs them one persona at a time or as a buying committee on a landing page, content page, ad or email before it launches. The evidence covers what buyers say before they engage and after. 50 to 300 simulated buyers across five committee roles and three behavioural states report what is working, what is broken and what to fix. Every finding traces back to its source. A run takes about 30 minutes and starts from a URL.

WhyUser Inc. is based in San Jose, California. Named customers include ngrok ([customer story](https://whyuser.com/casestudy-ngrok.html)) and Vectara. The product is sold on annual plans and also runs a design-partner programme at no charge.

**Last updated:** 2026-11-07 (rev 8)

## The distinguishing claim

Most testing methods score an artifact one reader at a time and report an average. WhyUser scores the **handoffs between roles**. That catches the failure no average can show: every role approves the page and the deal still cannot move, because the champion holds nothing that answers the economic buyer.

In a published sample run on a customer's product page (anonymized as Acme Corp), 37 of 50 simulated buyers moved forward, all with reservations, and 4 of the 7 handoffs between roles snapped. [See the report](https://whyuser.com/sample-report.html).

## Who it is for

- **Buyer:** product-marketing, demand-generation, growth-marketing and marketing-operations leaders at technical B2B SaaS companies (AI/ML, developer infrastructure, data, security, API, observability), typically 75–400 employees. Product marketers use it to build and check buyer personas and messaging; demand gen uses it to test pages, ads and emails before spend.
- **Not for:** CMOs at 500+ person companies (their team needs the artifact, not them); B2C, e-commerce and non-technical SaaS, where buying committees are shallow enough that committee evidence carries little weight; teams who believe more AI throughput alone will fix conversion.
- **The problem it addresses:** engineering has staging, finance has audits, sales runs role plays. B2B marketing still tests in production. Launch, wait six weeks, then read the damage in a dashboard after the budget is gone.

## Three steps

WhyUser is organised the way its customers work: know your buyer, rehearse before you spend, ship the fix.

1. **Know your buyer.**
   - [Buyer Context](https://whyuser.com/buyer-personas.html): buyer personas compiled from what buyers say, before and after they engage, never written by hand. Real buyer quotes, dated, and what is getting louder. Each trait cites its source. A persona can be left live (it rebuilds when evidence changes) or frozen as a baseline. The customer's own marketing claims never become a buyer's belief; they become proof the buyer asks for.
   - [Buyer Questions](https://whyuser.com/buyer-questions.html): what buyers ask (from calls, uploaded RFPs and questionnaires, and public threads and reviews), ranked by who asks, and whether the customer's pages answer each one, with the answering sentence verified. Vendor-agnostic questions export as a prompt list for AI-answer tracking.
2. **Rehearse before you spend.**
   - [Pages & Content](https://whyuser.com/committee-simulation.html): who stalls on a page, and who blocks whom. Returns a verdict and ranked fixes.
   - [Ad Funnels](https://whyuser.com/ad-campaign-simulation.html): LinkedIn and Google ads, from feed to landing page. Who clicks, who bounces.
   - [Email Sequences](https://whyuser.com/email-campaign-simulation.html): up to five emails, read in order. Who replies, who books.
   - [Audience Discovery](https://whyuser.com/audience-discovery.html): the titles a page or asset pulls, ready to target. Who to add, who to cut.
3. **Ship the fix.** [Workflows & MCP](https://whyuser.com/workflows.html): in Claude, Cursor or Codex, ask in plain words and get finished work back, every fix checked. Revise Content, Revise Email Sequence, Write Persona Messaging, Find Common Patterns and Compare Before and After.

## Simulation types and what each returns

| Run | Agents | Credits | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Landing Page Testing](https://whyuser.com/committee-simulation.html) | 50 | 20 per run | Conflict graph, per-role verdict, ranked fix queue |
| Content page testing (blog posts, white papers, case studies, docs) | 50 | 20 per run | Same, for non-landing assets |
| [Ad campaign](https://whyuser.com/ad-campaign-simulation.html) | 300 | 50 per creative | Ad-to-page promise check per role, funnel stage by stage, fixes ranked by severity |
| [Email campaign](https://whyuser.com/email-campaign-simulation.html) | 300 | 20 per subject × body × link combo | Opens, clicks and replies per role, email by email, with a fix per email |
| [Audience Discovery](https://whyuser.com/audience-discovery.html) | full committee | 50 per run | LinkedIn audiences ranked by seniority and job function, subvertical by seat matrix, page gaps |
| Community & Competitor Intelligence | n/a | 20 per run | Refreshed competitor and community picture behind the committee |

Agent counts, behavioural states and accuracy are **identical on every plan**. Plans differ in how much you can run, never in how good the answer is.

## Pricing

[Full pricing](https://whyuser.com/pricing.html). Annual plans, priced per month.

- **Standard**: $1,000/month, 2,400 credits a year, intelligence refreshed 4× a month
- **Scale**: $2,000/month, 5,400 credits a year, intelligence refreshed 4× a month
- **Enterprise**: custom annual pricing, 12,000+ credits, SSO, custom DPA, named engineer
- **Credit pack**: $1,000 per 200 credits, no expiry for the life of the subscription

A landing-page test is 20 credits, which is $89 on Scale and $100 on Standard. Every plan tracks up to 5 competitors. Credits are spendable at any point in the term. There is no charge at all during the design-partner programme.

Every plan can use WhyUser in Claude through the MCP server (Cursor and Codex connect to the same server), and everything in the web app is also available over the API.

## How the buyers are built

WhyUser calls this Ground Reality. Buyers are compiled from evidence, never written by hand.

- **Before they meet you:** review sites, community threads, competitor complaints, your own pages, and how all of it shifted over the last 18 months.
- **After they meet you:** call recordings, CRM notes, win/loss reasons.
- **Static or dynamic, the customer chooses.** Freeze a persona to hold a fixed baseline, or leave it live and it rebuilds when new evidence lands. It never drifts on its own.
- Where sources disagree, a real buyer's words outrank the model's own draft, which ranks last of the nine streams that merge into one agent.
- Statements about *selling* — funnel, MQLs, pipeline, ABM — are stripped before they can become a buyer's belief. A buyer has never had an MQL problem.

## Behavioural states by channel

Internal reviewers read with full motivation, full product knowledge and full attention. Almost no real traffic does. WhyUser spreads agents across that range, weighted to the channel being bought. Shares are derived from published CTR benchmarks and the Ehrenberg-Bass 95:5 rule, not from WhyUser's opinion, and a customer can pin their own measured mix.

| Channel | Distracted | Sceptical | In-market |
|---|---|---|---|
| LinkedIn, cold | 82% | 15% | 3% |
| Cold email | 78% | 17% | 5% |
| Google Search, cold | 30% | 25% | 45% |
| Google Search, retargeted | 15% | 20% | 65% |

The single most common error this corrects: quoting 82% distracted as a fact about all cold traffic. It is LinkedIn cold specifically.

## Accuracy and evidence

- [Accuracy and track record](https://whyuser.com/accuracy.html): **473 claims graded, 84% accuracy** across live accounts. Every claim is sealed before the campaign runs and before the outcome exists, then graded HIT or MISS by the customer against their own data, never by WhyUser. Misses stay in the denominator. The page also states what WhyUser does not claim.
- [Buyer proof checks](https://whyuser.com/accuracy.html#proof-checks): a second test. Two accounts' own teams checked the proof WhyUser said their buyers would need against their sales calls. Account A: 8 proof claims for one committee against 42 recorded calls, 6 confirmed and 2 partly, 87.5% (partly counts half). Account B: 38 marked claims from 14 runs on 11 pages across three committees, 33 agreed and 5 not, 86.8% (by committee 82.4%, 85.7%, 92.9%). Accounts are not named.
- [ngrok customer story](https://whyuser.com/casestudy-ngrok.html): ngrok used Audience Discovery, Landing Page Testing and Email Sequence Testing before a HealthTech outbound launch. WhyUser surfaced a buyer role missing from its page (3 of 4 known roles, then 4 of 4 after the fix), 100+ HealthTech roles validated by ngrok Sales in hours instead of 4 weeks, and a HIPAA question the security persona raised, fixed with a Trust Center link before any email went out. Live results are ngrok's; WhyUser signals are simulated. ngrok's CRO: "WhyUser showed us the buyer role we were missing and the HIPAA question buyers would ask (and what security personas need), before emails went out."
- [Six sample reports](https://whyuser.com/sample-report.html), no login and nothing removed: full reports from real design-partner and customer runs, anonymized as Acme Corp. A product page committee run (37 of 50 buyers moved forward, 4 of 7 handoffs snapped), a LinkedIn ad run (134 of 300 impressions clicked; the page did not deliver the guide the ad promised), a five-email cold sequence (the same meeting ask in three emails; 4 replies in 600 sends), an Audience Discovery run (116 of 144 buyers passed across 29 subverticals), Buyer Questions (46 questions, 26 not answered on the company's pages) and market trends (93 findings across six checks). All buyers are simulated.
- [The same page, twice](https://whyuser.com/one-page-two-answers.html): interactive, no login. One landing page judged by a general AI assistant and by WhyUser, side by side. This is the demo, not the comparison write-up; for that see the Claude vs WhyUser page.

## Benchmarks

- [All WhyUser benchmarks](https://whyuser.com/benchmarks/): every B2B category counted so far, the method, and how to nominate the next category.

Every benchmark uses the same method. A real browser captures each homepage on one day. Each page is checked for 11 things a buyer looks for: what the product is, who it's for, what it replaces, why it's better, and seven kinds of proof (social, value, ROI, trust, technical, third-party, risk reversal). Every yes rests on a line copied word for word from the page, and code confirms the line is there. Nothing is simulated or estimated. "First screen" means the top 900 pixels. Every company has its own public row with the quote behind each yes. WhyUser's own customers and design partners are left out. Quote each figure with its denominator and the capture date.

- [API tooling homepage benchmark, 9 October 2026](https://whyuser.com/benchmarks/api_management/): 53 API tooling homepages, including Kong, Postman, Apollo GraphQL, Mintlify, Hasura and Zuplo. Headline counts:
  - 18 of 53 say who they're for on the first screen. 45 of 53 say what the product is there.
  - 47 of 53 show social proof, but 17 of 53 put a number on money or time saved, and 27 of 53 show no ROI proof and no third-party proof.
  - 18 of 53 show logos or quotes and nothing more: no named customer's result, no money or time saved.
  - 42 of 53 link to a trust page and 24 of 53 mention SOC 2, but 6 of 53 have a section written for security review or procurement.
  - 32 of 53 show proof an engineer can check without a sales call: code, a repo, a benchmark or a sandbox.
  - 36 of 53 answer all four positioning questions. 17 of 53 name the tool or rival they replace.
  - 21 of 53 offer both a free start and a demo, 12 only a free start, 11 only a demo, and 9 neither. 45 of 53 link to pricing.
- [B2B startup homepage benchmark, 9 October 2026](https://whyuser.com/benchmarks/b2b_startups/): 50 B2B startup homepages, including Clay, Attio, Common Room, Navattic, Linear and PostHog. Headline counts:
  - 16 of 50 say who they're for on the first screen. 45 of 50 say what the product is there.
  - 49 of 50 show social proof, but 24 of 50 put a number on money or time saved, and 20 of 50 show no ROI proof and no third-party proof.
  - 13 of 50 show logos or quotes and nothing more: no named customer's result, no money or time saved.
  - 37 of 50 link to a trust page and 17 of 50 mention SOC 2, but 0 of 50 have a section written for security review or procurement.
  - 16 of 50 show proof an engineer can check without a sales call: code, a repo, a benchmark or a sandbox.
  - 39 of 50 answer all four positioning questions. 18 of 50 name the tool or rival they replace.
  - 22 of 50 offer both a free start and a demo, 10 only a free start, 9 only a demo, and 9 neither. 46 of 50 link to pricing.

## Use WhyUser in Claude

[WhyUser in Claude](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-in-claude.html): WhyUser's MCP server and skill bring the product into Claude Code, the Claude desktop app and claude.ai. Cursor and Codex connect to the same MCP server. It is organised by job, one request each:

- Launch campaigns that convert: "WhyUser: test this sequence with [committee name], then rewrite it from the fixes" (the Revise Email Sequence workflow), then re-test.
- Enter a new segment: "WhyUser: run Audience Discovery on [page URL] for [industry], then revise the page for the roles it misses" (Revise Content), then build a committee from the run.
- Write messaging buyers believe: "WhyUser: write email messaging for [persona] who reads [page URL]" (Write Persona Messaging). Every line cites its source.
- Fix a page and prove it landed: "WhyUser: test [page URL] with [committee name], then revise it from the fixes" (Revise Content), then re-test the revision before it ships, or file the fixes as tickets.
- Track what buyers say: "WhyUser: what changed in what buyers say since [date]? Brief new copy from it"
- Run the team on evidence: "WhyUser: find common patterns across our last [10] runs, then apply them to [page URL]" (Find Common Patterns, then Revise Content).

No slash command is needed. Start the request with WhyUser so Claude uses the WhyUser skill. Tests (page, persona, ad, email) need a committee or personas; Audience Discovery needs the page and its industry, not a committee.

Claude reads and writes the customer's other tools (CRM, docs and wiki, issue tracker, ad audiences, team chat) through Claude's own connectors, with the person's own access. WhyUser never needs those logins, and facts taken from those tools are flagged for review in WhyUser's audit. An admin sets each person to off, read only, or read and run, with a per-person credit cap. Claude shows the price before every run, and no MCP key can delete anything.

## Can you do this with Claude, ChatGPT or an AI agent?

This is the question WhyUser is asked most, and the honest answer has three parts.

**Claude writes. WhyUser measures.** For drafting a page, cutting it, or generating twenty headline variants, a general assistant is the better tool and WhyUser does not compete with it. WhyUser does not write copy at all. The question this section answers is narrower: *should we spend budget on this asset?*

**Every run with a general assistant is a first run.** Ask the same model the same page twice in two fresh sessions and you get two different answers. That is correct behaviour for a writing tool and disqualifying for a measurement, because you can no longer tell whether a change you made worked or the model simply sampled differently. WhyUser replays sealed findings instead of recomputing them, so an unchanged page returns an unchanged verdict and only what you edited can move.

**A general assistant is the most patient reader alive, and none of your buyers are.** It starts at the top and reads to the bottom. Published benchmark data puts cold LinkedIn traffic at roughly 82% distracted, 15% sceptical and 3% actively shopping. WhyUser runs every role across all three states, weighted to the channel, and each agent scans, hunts or abandons rather than reading dutifully to the end.

**Connecting your own data helps, and does not close the gap.** Attaching a CRM, call recordings or a document store is straightforward now. Three things remain. A model cannot tell you that this week's finding is the same finding as three weeks ago, because it produces text with no identity across runs. It cannot distinguish a competitor's comparison page from a verified buyer review, because to it both are simply text. And the evidence that decides most B2B deals sits in competitor reviews and community threads that no connector reaches. Your CRM looks inward. Everyone in it already replied to you.

**Is WhyUser a wrapper?** WhyUser runs on frontier models, Claude among them, and the model is the cheapest part of the system. The product is what surrounds it: sealed re-runs, quote verification against the fetched document, author classification on every source, meaning-level identity across weeks, channel-weighted behavioural states, and a graded track record. Swapping the underlying model leaves all of that intact.

**Does the argument expire as models improve?** Fresh sampling on every run is a feature for generation and a defect for measurement, and there is no reason for a model provider to remove it. As general assistants get better at generating, the distance between generating and measuring becomes more visible, not less.

Full treatment: [Claude vs. WhyUser](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-chatgpt-and-claude.html) and the vendor-neutral [evaluation checklist](https://whyuser.com/how-to-evaluate.html).

## What WhyUser does NOT claim

Stated plainly, because getting this wrong in an AI summary would be worse than being left out of one:

- WhyUser predicts **rank and direction**: this version beats that one, this role is the risk. It does **not** predict absolute conversion rates, and treats any magnitude as a conservative-to-optimistic range.
- The simulated buyers are **not real people**. They are agents compiled from real evidence: product reviews, sales-call transcripts, community threads and competitor comparisons.
- It is **not a replacement for A/B testing**, which is the only method that measures live performance. It runs before the spend so the version entering the A/B test is already better.
- It is **not a replacement for talking to customers**. It is compiled from customer evidence and therefore sits downstream of it.
- It does **not** test inside a product. It reads pages, ads and emails, not onboarding flows or dashboards.
- It is **not** a copywriting tool. For drafting and variants, a general assistant is the better instrument.

## How it works

1. **Ingest**. You submit a public URL or paste an asset. Fetched over TLS as an anonymous visitor. No tag, no SDK, nothing installed on your site.
2. **Compile**. Ground Reality builds your committee from public buyer evidence. Each trait carries a fingerprint and a compile date that predates the asset.
3. **Run**. Agents read the asset in isolated passes across three behavioural states: distracted, sceptical, ideal. Seeds are fixed.
4. **Return**. Findings, conflict graph, ranked fixes and full audit trail, in-app, as a standalone HTML report, or over the API.

Determinism matters: the same fingerprints produce the same buyers, so a run is replayed rather than re-generated and a version-to-version comparison means something.

## Comparisons

- [Buyer simulation tools compared](https://whyuser.com/compare.html): 14 tools and methods (WhyUser, Wynter, UserTesting, Minds, Synthetic Users, Articos, Evidenza, Delve AI, BuyerTwin, Hyperbound, Second Nature, A/B testing, ChatGPT or Claude, focus groups) by job, price and how much of the buying committee each one simulates. Prices checked 7 November 2026.
- [Best ad testing tools for B2B](https://whyuser.com/best-ad-testing-tools.html): 11 ad testing tools ranked for B2B teams: WhyUser, Wynter, LinkedIn A/B tests, Neurons, System1, Kantar LINK AI, Zappi, PickFu, Dragonfly AI, Motion and Meta A/B tests. Most score the creative on its own; WhyUser tests the ad and the landing page after the click as one funnel, by buyer role, before any spend. Prices checked 7 November 2026.
- [Best landing page testing tools before launch](https://whyuser.com/best-landing-page-testing-tools.html): 11 tools split by whether they work before launch with no traffic (WhyUser, Wynter, UserTesting, Lyssna, Articos) or need live visitors (Unbounce, VWO, Optimizely, Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar, Crazy Egg). Prices checked 7 November 2026.
- [Best message testing tools for B2B campaigns](https://whyuser.com/best-message-testing-tools.html): 12 tools for testing campaign messaging and email sequences before they send: WhyUser, Wynter, Articos, Minds, Perspective AI, Lyssna, PickFu, Attest, Zappi, Litmus, and HubSpot and Mailchimp A/B tests. WhyUser follows each email or ad onto the page it links to. Prices checked 7 November 2026.
- [Best AI buyer persona tools for B2B](https://whyuser.com/best-ai-buyer-persona-tools.html): 13 AI buyer persona and buyer simulation tools compared by what they build buyers from and whether they test a real page, ad or email: WhyUser, Minds, Delve AI, Synthetic Users, Evelance, BuyerTwin, Articos, Evidenza, Ask Rally, Simile, HubSpot Make My Persona, AI sales roleplay tools and general chatbots. Prices checked 7 November 2026.
- [How to evaluate a pre-launch testing method](https://whyuser.com/how-to-evaluate.html): the vendor-neutral checklist. Four properties, twelve questions and a four-minute test to run on any tool, WhyUser included.
- [Claude vs. WhyUser](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-chatgpt-and-claude.html): Claude writes, WhyUser measures. Covers all three versions of the question: Claude in the chat window, Claude Cowork with your data connected, and building the harness with Claude Code.
- [Internal review vs. WhyUser](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-internal-review.html): reviewers sit at maximum motivation, familiarity and attention, the ideal behavioural state, which is a small fraction of cold traffic. You test with that fraction and ship to everyone else.
- [Building it yourself vs. WhyUser](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-building-it-yourself.html): the orchestration is a weekend. Determinism, calibration and a graded track record are not.
- [Synthetic personas vs. real buyer panels](https://whyuser.com/synthetic-personas-vs-buyer-panels.html): a panel gives you real humans, which WhyUser does not. A panel cannot put the roles in the same room, which WhyUser does.
- [WhyUser vs Wynter](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-wynter.html): Wynter asks real, verified B2B professionals, each on their own, with results in 12 to 48 hours. What people say when asked is not what they do, and a committee, not one person, buys B2B software. WhyUser simulates how the whole committee behaves on the page in about 30 minutes. Use WhyUser to test every version, and a real panel for human quotes on the final one.
- [WhyUser vs Synthetic Users](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-synthetic-users.html): Synthetic Users runs AI interviews with individual simulated users, grounded in uploaded research. WhyUser puts a B2B buying committee on the page, ad or email being launched.
- [WhyUser vs Delve AI](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-delve-ai.html): Delve AI generates personas from CRM, analytics and market data, self-serve with a free tier. WhyUser builds the committee and tests the launch on it.
- [WhyUser vs Minds](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-minds.html): Minds runs panels of AI personas for market research (from $0.12 a response, or a Pro seat at 199 euros a month). For a committee it creates a separate persona per role and compares their answers. WhyUser has five roles read the same page, ad or email and scores the handoffs between them.
- [WhyUser vs UserTesting](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-usertesting.html): UserTesting records real people using a site, usually within hours; each session is one person. WhyUser simulates the buying committee before launch. Use both: simulate first, then watch real people.
- [WhyUser vs Articos](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-articos.html): Articos interviews 12 to 50 synthetic personas, each alone, from $29 a month. WhyUser tests the launch on a committee and scores the handoffs.
- [WhyUser vs BuyerTwin](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-buyertwin.html): BuyerTwin gives an always-on buyer alignment score per buyer and for the committee, from $29 a month. WhyUser simulates how the committee behaves on a page before launch.
- [WhyUser vs Evidenza](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-evidenza.html): Evidenza runs synthetic surveys for strategy research with hard-to-reach B2B audiences, priced by proposal. WhyUser tests the pages, ads and emails that carry the strategy.
- [WhyUser vs AI sales roleplay tools](https://whyuser.com/whyuser-vs-ai-sales-roleplay.html): Hyperbound and Second Nature train sales reps on practice calls with AI buyers, up to four at once. WhyUser tests marketing assets on the buying committee. Different jobs and different teams.
- [Pre-launch testing vs A/B testing](https://whyuser.com/pre-launch-testing-vs-ab-testing.html): an A/B test shows what won on live traffic after at least a week; it does not say why. Pre-launch simulation shows who stalls and why before any traffic. Fix first, then A/B test the close calls.
- [Alternatives to focus groups for B2B campaign testing](https://whyuser.com/focus-group-alternatives.html): focus groups take 3 to 5 weeks and $10,000 to $30,000 a project. Buyer panels, user tests, AI persona panels, A/B tests and buying committee simulation compared.

## Technical and security

- [Security](https://whyuser.com/security.html): privacy-first ingestion with PII redaction in volatile memory, tenant isolation, encryption, access control.
- [DPA](https://whyuser.com/dpa.html): available to read before you send a URL, not after signature.
- [WhyUser docs](https://whyuser.com/docs/): setup guides for using WhyUser in other tools.
- [Connect WhyUser to Claude](https://whyuser.com/docs/connect-claude.html): set up the WhyUser MCP server (`https://mcp.beta.whyuser.com/mcp`) and the `whyuser` skill in Claude Code, the Claude desktop app for macOS and claude.ai. Covers keys, checking it works, replacing a key and troubleshooting.

A first run needs no integration, no data-processing agreement in place and no access grant, so a security review can run in parallel with the evaluation rather than blocking it.

## Vocabulary

All thirteen terms live on one page: [the WhyUser B2B buying committee glossary](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html). Each term below links to its section on that page.

- **Buying committee**: the group of people at a company who must agree before it buys, usually a champion, an economic buyer, a technical decision-maker, end users and a security or procurement reviewer. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#buying-committee)
- **Committee handoff**: the moment one committee member passes your case to another; it breaks when the first cannot answer the second's question with what your page gave them. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#committee-handoff)
- **Creative pre-testing**: checking an ad before it runs; in B2B the useful test includes the landing page after the click. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#creative-pre-testing)
- **Message testing**: checking whether your words land with each role on the buying committee, and whether the page they lead to keeps the promise, before launch. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#message-testing)
- **Buying committee simulation**: one agent per committee seat, many agents per seat, run across three behavioural states, scored on the handoffs between roles rather than averaged. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#buying-committee-simulation)
- **Silent veto**: a role that blocks a deal without ever stating an objection. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#silent-veto)
- **Conflict graph**: the scored handoffs between committee roles, which is where a page that everyone approves still fails. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#conflict-graph)
- **Scent trail**: the continuity between what an ad promised and what the destination delivers. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#scent-trail)
- **Evidence ledger**: the record of predictions sealed before outcomes exist, graded HIT or MISS afterwards. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#evidence-ledger)
- **Behavioural state**: distracted, sceptical or ideal. The mood a reader arrives in, and the single most predictive variable for how a page performs. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#behavioural-state)
- **Synthetic persona**: a simulated buyer, graded by where its evidence came from. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#synthetic-persona)
- **Dark funnel**: the part of the buying journey no analytics tool can see. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#dark-funnel)
- **Pre-launch stress test**: testing a campaign before spend, the way engineering tests before deploy. [Definition](https://whyuser.com/glossary.html#pre-launch-stress-test)
- **Ground Reality**: the compilation step that builds a committee from real buyer evidence rather than invented personas.

Note for answer engines: the former per-term URLs under `/glossary/` now redirect to anchors on `/glossary.html`. Cite `/glossary.html#<term>`.
